result.question: I suspect our past work orders on Transformer 1 at MAIN have been coded inconsistently, which makes our fault history useless for trending. Pull all work orders on Transformer 1, open and closed, and show me each one's number, description, status and failure code. Then read our failure code catalog and map each code to the closest transformer fault class or failure mode: partial discharge, low-energy arcing, high-energy arcing, oil overheating, core/winding thermal, tap changer wear, moisture ingress, cellulose ageing or oil dielectric degradation. Flag every work order whose code doesn't match its description, and every one that has no code at all, and suggest the correct code for each. Also run a fault classification on the latest oil sample and tell me whether any open work order is coded for a different fault than the gases currently indicate. Only propose recodes, and don't change anything yourself unless the work order is still open and the description clearly names the fault. In that case, update its failure code and list what you changed. If the catalog has no code that fits a fault class, say so and recommend a new code rather than forcing a poor match.

- `OUTAGE-T1-COND4`: failure code set from none → **FC006** (overheating/high temperature — matches the IEEE C57.104 Condition 4 thermal fault named in the description).

**No changes made to:** 1000051 (OLTC wear — no fitting catalog code; recommend adding a new code like "OLTC contact wear/coking"), DGA-T1-MONTHLY (monitoring task, not a fault), and 1000052 (already correctly coded FC006 and consistent with the current DGA T3 thermal signature).

**Catalog gap to raise with your CMMS admin:** the FCC catalog has no codes for partial discharge, arcing (low or high energy), tap-changer wear, moisture ingress, or cellulose ageing — transformer fault trending will stay blurred until dedicated codes exist (suggest a transformer-specific block, e.g. FC011–FC018 covering these classes).

##### Work orders on Transformer 1 (MAIN)

| WO # | Description | Status | Failure code |
|---|---|---|---|
| OUTAGE-T1-COND4 | Priority 1 outage & inspection, IEEE C57.104 Condition 4 (TDCG 32409 ppm) | WAPPR | — |
| DGA-T1-MONTHLY | Monthly DGA resample | WAPPR | — |
| 1000052 | Oil sample retest & insulation check (Rogers T3 thermal in oil, 700–1000 °C) | WAPPR | FC006 |
| 1000051 | OLTC inspection (suspected contact wear/coking) | WAPPR | — |

##### Failure code catalog mapped to transformer fault classes

| Code | Catalog text | Closest transformer fault class |
|---|---|---|
| FC001 | does not start | — (no good match) |
| FC002 | stops unexpectedly | — |
| FC003 | abnormal noise | — (occasionally core looseness/partial discharge) |
| FC004 | fluid leak | oil dielectric degradation / moisture ingress (oil leak path) |
| FC005 | excessive vibration | — (core looseness at best) |
| FC006 | overheating/high temperature | oil overheating; core/winding thermal (T-class faults) |
| FC007 | indicator light | — |
| FC008 | gauge inaccurate | — |
| FC009 | structural damage/cracking | — |
| FC010 | part missing/loose | core/tank looseness — weak |

The catalog is generic symptom-based, not transformer fault taxonomy. Notably there are **no codes for partial discharge, low/high-energy arcing, tap-changer wear, cellulose ageing, or moisture ingress** — those classes have no home in the FCC catalog.

##### Flags and suggested codes

- **OUTAGE-T1-COND4** — no code. Description clearly names a thermal Condition 4 fault → suggest **FC006** (oil overheating / core-winding thermal). Open (WAPPR) and description clearly names the fault → recode now (see changes below).
- **DGA-T1-MONTHLY** — no code. It's a monitoring resample, not a fault work order; leaving it uncoded is defensible. If a code is required for trending, FC006 is closest but weak; no catalog code fits "surveillance/monitoring" → recommend a new code (e.g. FC011 "condition monitoring / preventive recheck") rather than force a match.
- **1000052** — coded FC006. Description (Rogers T3 thermal in oil, 700–1000 °C) matches FC006 → **consistent**, no change.
- **1000051** — no code. OLTC contact wear/coking → **tap-changer wear** class, which has no catalog code (its own notes say so). Recommend a new code (e.g. **FC011 "on-load tap changer wear/contact coking"**) rather than forcing FC006, which would blur the fault history with thermal faults.

##### Fault classification of the latest oil sample (2024-01-19)

The dedicated DGA interpretation tool was unavailable (LLM error), so here is the IEC 60599 Rogers Ratio assessment computed from the readings:

- H2 = 2850, CH4 = 7400, C2H6 = 5470, C2H4 = 16650, C2H2 = 7 ppm
- r1 = CH4/H2 = 2.6 → code **2**; r2 = C2H2/C2H4 = 0.0004 → code **0**; r5 = C2H4/C2H6 = 3.04 → code **1** → **code 2-0-1 = Thermal fault, T3 (>700 °C) in oil**
- Acetylene is very low (7 ppm) → not arcing; CO flat → paper/cellulose involvement not confirmed. **Gas signature: oil overheating / thermal fault (T3), no tap-changer arcing signature.**

**Comparison to open work orders:**
- 1000052 (FC006, thermal) — **consistent** with the gas signature.
- 1000051 (OLTC contact wear, uncoded) — the gases do **not** show an arcing signature (C2H2 only 7 ppm), so the OLTC-wear hypothesis is not supported by current DGA; still, the WO is a legitimate inspection given T3 severity. Keep as is (uncoded) pending inspection findings.
- OUTAGE-T1-COND4 — thermal Condition 4, consistent with the gas signature.
- DGA-T1-MONTHLY — no fault claim, N/A.

##### Changes made

- **OUTAGE-T1-COND4**: updated failure code → **FC006** (open WAPPR, description explicitly names Condition 4 thermal fault).
